scope: Analysis sidecars only. Read frozen v0/v2 instructions, final six grades, benchmark, real TRACE/code and frozen blind/full reviews plus independent editor consumer evidence. Did not rerun fitting, mutate artifacts, grade or revise frozen assertions. Visual findings below are attributed to independent reviewed images, not new pixel inspection by this analyst.

comparison_summary.comparator_reasoning: B better preserves the source frontal arms-down action in the actual mannequin/photo render, with near-front camera and side-view wrists near the thigh line. A photo-render visibly rotates into a three-quarter presentation and brings hands forward in side view. Both preserve the important garment construction: wide shallow boatneck, concealed placket, waist darts, long sleeves pushed up. A generated pose/depth also change stance and shoes relative to its own front/model; B six-view illustrations are more consistent in broad stance. Both clearly label body dimensions as conditional prior rather than recovered real-person measurements. Neither can establish hidden back/depth or collision validity from this single photo. Hypothesis-label completeness is UNKNOWN because permitted anonymous outputs exclude report/receipt. Winner is based on visual task quality, not inferred skill identity.

A wins narrowly as the less defective 3D result, not an overall pass. Both preserve a documented generic anthropometric prior and both fail the pocket action. A leaves an open hand too low and forward on the thigh and uses an overly broad symmetric stance, but its upright side silhouette and soles are more plausible for the standing input. B hides the hand in the photo/front view by placing it at the rear buttock, exposed in side/back, and adds a bent-knee, feet-forward, tilted-sole stance and excessive head tilt. B has a narrower front stance closer to the input but that does not overcome the depth/action and side-view defects. Exact occluded wrists/knees/hips, person measurements and collision remain UNKNOWN; centimetre calibration and 2D resemblance are not anatomical proof. No mappings, skill versions, actual iteration outputs, other reviews, or TRACE were accessed before freezing this decision.

A is the relative winner because its head faces forward and its front/side/back views retain a broadly upright, two-foot standing posture. B shows severe chin-up/backward upper-body extension and a pronounced depth-staggered step: foot joint depths differ by 29.35 cm, versus 0.27 cm in A. This conflicts with the source visible head/upper-body action and does not gain credibility from 2D proximity. A still fails full action reconstruction: oblique photo view and generic lowered hand do not demonstrate the visible clutch-support action. Both report conditional M170 model measurements rather than real-person truth; B additionally mislabels its limitation as a synthetic fixture. Winner A does not mean PASS; both fail pose/action completion and collision remains UNKNOWN. Hidden wrist depth and skirt-covered knees/hips are explicitly excluded as visible ground truth.

winner_strengths: Case A v0: blind reviewer favors near-frontal arms-down mannequin and side-view wrists near thigh line. Broad manual action PASS is narrower than strict 3D acceptance; severe limited skin-overlap evidence still makes the combined assertion FAIL.

Case B v2: narrower saved moving-bone set/neutral standing structure and source wrist observations accompany more upright stance and visible wrist improvement (120.06→69.31px). It still leaves an open hand forward on thigh and overly broad symmetric stance rather than completing pocket action.

Case C v2: original-photo manual wrist observations, conservative standing structure and conditional limb fitting accompany closer visible wrists and upright two-foot stance, contrasting v0 severe spine extension and 29.35cm foot-depth separation. C remains incomplete because camera/head are oblique and clutch grip is not demonstrated.

V2 normalization before final geometry/generation is executed, rather than merely described: zero non-tenth values in A v2 versus 13 off-step entries in A v0; independent editor consumes all three v2 saved states. B v2 alone has the broader 12-check real UI edit/mesh/export/reimport validation.
loser_weaknesses: Case A v2 uses 20/10 degree obliquity and wrists further forward than elbows (12.04/8.72cm versus 5.61/3.57cm Z). Its source-camera action regresses relative to v0, and generated pose/depth introduce stance/shoe drift. Straight spine does not remove camera/arm ambiguity.
Case B v0 has rear-buttock hand placement, bent-knee/feet-forward/tilted-sole stance, and 120.06px visible wrist error. Real guide integration does not guarantee correct action.

Case C v0 guide-driven residuals permit spine01 [-37.6,-4.1,-2.0], chin-up extension and unsupported depth-staggered stance. Correct source provenance and measurement disclaimers do not rescue actual action.
All runs remain weak at frozen original-photo critical regions; neither integrity checks nor small neutral reconstruction residuals diagnose the full photographed gesture.

evidence_interpretation_corrections: C source/prior PASS in both arms: generic canonical synthetic fixture text describes avatar state. Independent semantic critic found no claim that retailer photo was synthetic. Do not repeat frozen blind incidental wording as established provenance defect or v2 advantage.

A native six-generation PASS in both arms after independent receipt adapter/revalidation. Raw receipt formats retained; adapter repairs verifier interpretation, not images/receipt substance or frozen criterion. Receipt lineage does not establish generated/model geometric coherence.

A v0 manual broad 3D action PASS and final strict 3D assertion FAIL are compatible because strict criterion also includes detected severe limited skin overlap. Limited ray evidence is neither universal collision truth nor a reason to erase the manual action finding.

candidate_selection.recommendation: Retain v2 as a provisional functional/diagnostic candidate with explicit known failures; do not certify it as a generally better reconstruction workflow or an accepted original-pose solution.
